questions.questionText: According to Newton's First Law, an object at rest will stay at rest unless acted upon by what?
questions.explanation: Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia): an object at rest stays at rest unless acted by external force

questions.questionText: What is the formula for Newton's Second Law?
questions.explanation: F = ma where F is force, m is mass, a is acceleration

questions.questionText: A car accelerates from 0 to 60 m/s in 10 seconds. What is its acceleration?
What is the acceleration due to gravity on Earth?
questions.explanation: g = 9.8 m/s² (approximately 10 m/s² for simplified calculations)

questions.questionText: A 2 kg object moving at 3 m/s has what momentum?
The kinetic energy equation is:
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv² where m is mass, v is velocity

questions.questionText: A force of 50 N moves an object 4 m. How much work is done?
A machine does 500 J of work in 10 seconds. What is its power?
A 10 N box slides on a surface with μ = 0.3. What is the frictional force?
A vector has both:
questions.explanation: Vectors have both magnitude and direction; scalars have only magnitude

questions.questionText: A book sitting on a table has how many forces acting on it?
questions.explanation: Weight (downward) and normal force from table (upward) = 2 forces

questions.questionText: A ball thrown horizontally from a height will land:

options.text: At the same time as if dropped

questions.hint: Horizontal and vertical motion are independent
questions.explanation: Both have same vertical motion, so hit ground simultaneously

questions.questionText: The force keeping a satellite in orbit is:
questions.explanation: Gravity provides centripetal force to keep satellite in orbit

questions.questionText: Density is calculated as:
questions.explanation: ρ = m/V

questions.questionText: Pressure is defined as:
questions.explanation: P = F/A

questions.questionText: Sound is what type of wave?
questions.explanation: Sound needs a medium (mechanical) and vibrates parallel to direction (longitudinal)

questions.questionText: Light travels fastest in:
questions.explanation: Light travels fastest in vacuum (c = 3×10⁸ m/s)

questions.questionText: Angle of incidence equals:
questions.explanation: θᵢ = θᵣ (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection)

questions.questionText: When light enters water from air, it:

options.text: Slows down and bends toward normal
Speeds up and bends toward normal

questions.explanation: Light slows in denser medium and bends toward the normal

questions.questionText: Heat transfer by convection occurs in:
questions.explanation: Convection transfers heat through fluid motion (liquids and gases)

questions.questionText: Conduction transfers heat best through:
questions.explanation: Metals are good conductors due to free electrons

questions.questionText: When heated, most materials:
questions.explanation: Heat increases particle motion, causing expansion

questions.questionText: Particles are closest together in:
questions.explanation: Solids have closely packed particles in fixed arrangement

questions.questionText: Electric field lines point away from:
questions.hint: Field direction is test charge direction
questions.explanation: Field lines point from positive to negative

questions.questionText: Current in a series circuit is:
questions.explanation: In series, same current flows through all components

questions.questionText: Ohm's Law states:
questions.explanation: V = IR (Voltage = Current × Resistance)

questions.questionText: Magnetic field lines outside a magnet go from:
questions.explanation: Lines go from North pole to South pole externally

questions.questionText: Current is induced when a magnet moves through a coil because:
questions.explanation: Changing magnetic flux induces EMF/current

questions.questionText: Most of an atom's mass is in the:
questions.explanation: Nucleus contains protons and neutrons (most of atomic mass)

questions.questionText: Alpha radiation consists of:
questions.explanation: Alpha particles are helium nuclei (₂He⁴)

questions.questionText: A sample has half-life of 10 years. After 30 years, fraction remaining is:
questions.explanation: After 10 yrs: 1/2, 20 yrs: 1/4, 30 yrs: 1/8

questions.questionText: A lever provides mechanical advantage by:
questions.explanation: Lever rotates around fulcrum to multiply force

questions.questionText: A falling object near Earth has approximately what acceleration?
questions.explanation: All objects near Earth accelerate at g = 9.8 m/s² (ignoring air resistance)

questions.questionText: The period of a pendulum depends on:
questions.explanation: Period T depends on length L and gravity g, not mass

questions.questionText: Energy can be:
questions.explanation: Law of Conservation: energy converted but total stays constant

questions.questionText: Which type of bond is formed when electrons are shared equally between two atoms of the same element?
questions.explanation: In non-polar covalent bonds, electrons are shared equally because the atoms have the same electronegativity.

questions.questionText: What effect does a catalyst have on a chemical reaction?
questions.explanation: A catalyst increases the reaction rate by providing an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.

questions.questionText: According to Le Chatelier's Principle, what happens to an exothermic reaction at equilibrium when temperature is increased?
questions.hint: System acts to oppose the change (remove heat)
questions.explanation: In an exothermic reaction, heat is a product. Increasing temperature adds heat, so the system shifts to the left to consume it.

questions.questionText: What is the IUPAC name for CH₃CH₂CH₂OH?
questions.hint: Count the carbons and identify the -OH position
questions.explanation: There are 3 carbons (prop-) and an alcohol group (-ol) on the first carbon.

questions.questionText: In a galvanic cell, oxidation occurs at the ____ which is the ____ electrode.
questions.hint: AN OX and RED CAT; and in Galvanic, Anode is negative
questions.explanation: Oxidation always occurs at the anode. In a galvanic cell, the anode is the negative electrode where electrons are released.

questions.questionText: Which intermolecular force is responsible for the unusually high boiling point of water?
questions.hint: It involves H bonded to N, O, or F
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonds are strong intermolecular forces occurring when H is bonded to highly electronegative atoms (N, O, F).

questions.questionText: To which homologous series does CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ belong?
questions.explanation: The -COO- group indicates an ester, formed from an acid and an alcohol.

questions.questionText: During the electrolysis of molten copper(II) chloride, what is produced at the cathode?
questions.hint: Positive ions (cations) migrate to the negative electrode
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ ions are attracted to the negative cathode, where they gain electrons (reduction) to form copper metal.

questions.questionText: What is the only factor that can change the value of the equilibrium constant (Kc)?
questions.hint: Stress only changes position, except for this one
questions.explanation: The equilibrium constant is temperature-dependent. Changes in concentration or pressure shift the position but not the constant.

questions.questionText: Which type of reaction converts an alkene into an alkane?
questions.hint: Breaking the double bond to add hydrogen
questions.explanation: Hydrogenation is an addition reaction where H₂ is added across the double bond of an alkene to form an alkane.

questions.questionText: VSEPR theory: What is the shape of a molecule with 4 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs on the central atom?
questions.explanation: Four bonding pairs arrange themselves as far apart as possible, forming a tetrahedral shape with 109.5° angles.

questions.questionText: How does increasing the surface area of a solid reactant affect the reaction rate?

options.text: Increases rate by providing more collision sites
Decreases rate by cooling the system

questions.explanation: A larger surface area allows more particles to be exposed to collisions, increasing the frequency of effective collisions.

questions.questionText: In the chlor-alkali industry, what are the three main products of the electrolysis of concentrated NaCl solution (brine)?
questions.hint: Cl₂ is produced at the anode, H₂ at the cathode
questions.explanation: The electrolysis of brine yields Cl₂ gas, H₂ gas, and NaOH solution (caustic soda).

questions.questionText: What is the general formula for the homologous series of alkanes?
questions.hint: Methane is CH₄, Ethane is C₂H₆
questions.explanation: Alkanes follow the general formula CnH2n+2, indicating they are saturated hydrocarbons.

questions.questionText: If the concentration of a reactant is increased in a system at equilibrium, the system will:
questions.explanation: Increasing reactant concentration causes the system to shift towards the products to consume the added reactant.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a structural isomer of butane?
questions.hint: Same molecular formula, different structural arrangement of carbon chain
questions.explanation: Both butane and 2-methylpropane have the molecular formula C₄H₁₀ but different carbon skeletons.

questions.questionText: What is the major product when 2-bromobutane reacts with concentrated NaOH in ethanol under reflux?
questions.hint: Concentrated base and ethanol favor elimination over substitution
questions.explanation: This is a dehydrohalogenation reaction (elimination). According to Zaitsev's rule, the more substituted alkene (but-2-ene) is the major product.

questions.questionText: In the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution curve, what does the total area under the curve represent?

options.text: Total number of particles in the sample
The activation energy of the reaction
The average kinetic energy of the particles
The rate of the chemical reaction

nodes.label: Shaded region: Particles with E >= Ea

questions.hint: Think about what the probability distribution covers
questions.explanation: The Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution shows the number of particles at different energies; hence the total area represents the total number of particles.

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly explains how an increase in temperature affects the reaction rate according to collision theory?

options.text: More particles have kinetic energy greater than or equal to Ea
The activation energy of the reaction is lowered
The particles become more concentrated in the vessel
The reaction becomes more exothermic, releasing more heat

questions.hint: Temperature relates to the speed and energy of particles
questions.explanation: Increased temperature increases average KE, resulting in a larger fraction of particles possessing sufficient energy (>= Ea) for effective collisions.

questions.questionText: If the equilibrium constant (Kc) for a reaction is 0.005 at 25°C, what does this indicate about the position of equilibrium?

options.text: The equilibrium lies far to the left (reactants favored)
The equilibrium lies far to the right (products favored)
The concentrations of reactants and products are equal

questions.explanation: A very small Kc value (< 1) means the denominator (reactants) is much larger than the numerator (products) at equilibrium.

questions.questionText: For the Haber Process: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) (ΔH = -92 kJ/mol). How will increasing the pressure of the system affect the yield of ammonia?
questions.hint: Le Chatelier's Principle: Increase in pressure favors the side with fewer gas moles
questions.explanation: There are 4 moles of gas on the left and 2 on the right. Increasing pressure shifts the equilibrium to the side with fewer moles (ammonia).

questions.questionText: According to the Brønsted-Lowry theory, an acid is defined as a:
questions.explanation: Brønsted-Lowry acids donate protons (H+), while bases accept them.

questions.questionText: What is the pH of a 0.001 mol/dm³ solution of nitric acid (HNO₃)?
questions.explanation: Nitric acid is a strong monoprotic acid, so [H+] = 0.001 mol/dm³. pH = -log(0.001) = 3.

questions.questionText: Which of the following standard reduction potentials (E°) represents the strongest oxidizing agent?
questions.hint: The more positive the E° value, the more easily the substance is reduced
questions.explanation: Strong oxidizing agents have the highest (most positive) reduction potentials because they have a high affinity for electrons.

questions.questionText: In a Zn-Cu galvanic cell, which of the following describes the movement of anions through the salt bridge?

options.text: Opposite to the direction of electrons in the bridge

questions.hint: Anions migrate to the Anode to balance the build-up of positive charge
questions.explanation: At the anode, oxidation produces Zn²⁺ ions. Negative anions from the salt bridge move into this half-cell to maintain electrical neutrality.

questions.questionText: What is the primary intermolecular force between molecules of propanone (acetone)?
questions.hint: Propanone has a polar C=O group but no O-H bond
questions.explanation: Ketones are polar due to the carbonyl group, leading to dipole-dipole interactions, but they cannot form hydrogen bonds with themselves.

questions.questionText: Which homologous series is characterized by the presence of a -CHO functional group?
questions.hint: It is always at the end of a carbon chain
questions.explanation: Aldehydes have the formyl group (-CHO) at the end of the chain. Ketones have -CO- in the middle.

questions.questionText: According to the collision theory, for a collision to be effective, particles must collide with:
questions.explanation: An effective collision requires the minimum activation energy and the correct geometric alignment to break and form bonds.

questions.questionText: If the rate law for a reaction is Rate = k[A][B]², what happens to the rate if the concentration of B is doubled?

options.text: It increases by a factor of 4
It increases by a factor of 8

questions.explanation: Since the reaction is second order with respect to B, doubling [B] results in a 2² = 4-fold increase in the rate.

questions.questionText: What happens to the Kc value of an endothermic reaction if the temperature is increased?
questions.hint: Increase in temp favors the endothermic direction
questions.explanation: For an endothermic reaction, increasing temperature shifts equilibrium to the right (products), which increases the Kc value.

questions.questionText: Which of the following will NOT affect the position of equilibrium for the reaction: H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g)?
questions.hint: Count the number of gas moles on each side
questions.explanation: There are 2 moles of gas on both sides, so pressure changes do not shift the equilibrium position.

questions.questionText: A solution of sodium ethanoate (CH₃COONa) is:
questions.hint: Consider the hydrolysis of the ethanoate ion
questions.explanation: CH₃COO⁻ is the conjugate base of a weak acid. It undergoes hydrolysis in water to produce OH⁻ ions, making the solution basic.

questions.questionText: Which indicator is most suitable for a titration between a strong acid and a weak base?
questions.hint: The equivalence point will be below pH 7
questions.explanation: A strong acid-weak base titration has an acidic equivalence point. Methyl orange changes color in the acidic range (pH 3.1-4.4).

questions.questionText: In an electrolytic cell, the cathode is the:
questions.hint: Reduction always happens at the cathode, but polarity differs from galvanic cells
questions.explanation: In electrolysis, an external source provides electrons to the cathode (negative), where reduction takes place.

questions.questionText: What is the function of the salt bridge in a galvanic cell?

options.text: To allow electrons to flow between half-cells
To provide a path for the external current

questions.explanation: The salt bridge completes the circuit and prevents charge build-up by allowing ions to migrate between the half-cells.

questions.questionText: Which property of alkanes explains why they are used as fuels?

options.text: They release large amounts of energy when burned
They are highly reactive with cold water
They have very high boiling points

questions.explanation: Alkanes undergo combustion reactions with oxygen, releasing significant thermal energy.

questions.questionText: Which type of isomerism is shown by but-1-ene and but-2-ene?
questions.hint: The position of the double bond changes
questions.explanation: They have the same carbon chain but the double bond is at different positions (C1 vs C2).

questions.questionText: A change in which factor will change the value of the rate constant (k)?
questions.explanation: The rate constant k is temperature-dependent. Higher temperatures lead to higher k values.

questions.questionText: The minimum energy required for a collision to result in a reaction is called:
questions.explanation: Activation energy is the 'barrier' that reactants must overcome to reach the transition state.

questions.questionText: What happens to the concentration of reactants when a catalyst is added to a system already at equilibrium?
questions.hint: Catalysts speed up both forward and reverse reactions equally
questions.explanation: A catalyst increases the rate at which equilibrium is reached but does not affect the position of equilibrium or the concentrations.

questions.questionText: In a reversible reaction, chemical equilibrium is reached when:

options.text: Rate of forward reaction equals rate of reverse reaction
Concentration of products equals concentration of reactants
All reactants have been converted to products

questions.explanation: At equilibrium, the rates are equal, and consequently, the concentrations of species remain constant.

questions.questionText: What is the conjugate acid of the base H₂O?
questions.hint: Add a proton (H+) to the base
questions.explanation: A conjugate acid is formed when a base accepts a proton. H₂O + H⁺ → H₃O⁺.

questions.questionText: A substance that can act as either an acid or a base is called:
questions.explanation: Ampholytes (like water or HSO₄⁻) can donate or accept protons depending on the environment.

questions.questionText: What is the standard cell potential (E°cell) for a cell with Zn/Zn²⁺ (-0.76 V) and Cu/Cu²⁺ (+0.34 V)?
questions.explanation: E°cell = 0.34 - (-0.76) = 1.10 V. Copper is the cathode (higher E°) and Zinc is the anode.

questions.questionText: Which statement is true for an object being electroplated with silver?

options.text: The object must be the cathode
The object must be the anode
The electrolyte must contain zinc ions
A silver rod is used as the cathode

questions.hint: The metal to be plated must be reduced onto the object
questions.explanation: The object to be plated is placed at the negative cathode where Ag⁺ ions from the solution gain electrons to form silver metal.
